about.title: Beverly Hills Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Beverly Hills is home to a concentration of private practices, cosmetic surgery centers, and specialty clinics, and most patients here receive excellent care. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgical step is skipped, or a medication error slips through, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law treats medical malpractice differently than an ordinary injury claim: strict notice periods, expert requirements, and damage rules under MICRA all apply. If you believe a Beverly Hills provider fell short of the accepted standard of care, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to review what happened. There's no obligation, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless your case results in a recovery. Understanding your options early matters, since some of these deadlines are shorter than people expect.

whyChoose.title: Why Beverly Hills Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Timeline
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into These Cases
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself isn't enough to prove malpractice; California requires a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. We connect you with attorneys who know how to line up that kind of review.

items.title: We Explain the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: California places a statutory cap on non-economic damages in malpractice cases, and that cap adjusts upward each year. An independent attorney can walk you through how that cap and other MICRA rules might apply to your specific situation.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. Before filing suit, California also requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Because these deadlines can be shorter than they sound, it helps to talk with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after cosmetic or elective surgery in Beverly Hills — is that automatically malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't establish malpractice; there has to be evidence that the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care. Given how many cosmetic and specialty practices operate in Beverly Hills, an independent attorney can help evaluate whether your case involves an actual breach of care.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California places a cap on non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in medical malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally handled separately. An attorney can explain how these categories apply to your specific circumstances.
